instruction: Select all images containing a house.

game.semantic_variant: Select all buildings that people live in.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary houses count, and so do the house standing on chicken legs and the house walking in boots: impossible, but still houses. The caravan carried by a tortoise and the hermit crab's brick house are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The office tower, the bus shelter and the shipping container are not houses.

correct: Houses identified. Please do not let them wander off.
Correct. Every house has been registered at its current address.
partial: Partially correct. A house appears to have moved.
Partially correct. Some houses are not at home.
incorrect: Incorrect. The houses have filed a complaint.
Incorrect. Your planning application has been refused.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary houses (pale-blue terraced house with a yellow door, front view; black timber cottage with yellow window frames, front three-quarter view), two impossible houses (generated red-brick house on two giant chicken legs in a meadow; generated white clapboard house standing in two giant leather boots on a street), two borderline dwellings (generated caravan riding on a giant tortoise at a campsite; generated hermit crab carrying a tiny brick house as its shell) and three non-member structures (glass office tower on a canal bank, rural bus shelter beside a field, faded white shipping container at a woodland edge). All non-members are buildings or shelters, so a roof and walls alone do not decide. Views, colours and settings vary within each role. The two detached houses, the white bungalow and the human-sized dollhouse remain in the collection for later versions.
